edits.english: And they shall not profane the holy things - There is no profanation when they offer them for the sake of an offering higher than themselves:

That are to be set apart - That is, untithed produce, as it is written: "they will set apart" [using] a future tense verb. And it concludes here in Sanhedrin, chapter "These are those who are burned," that the profanation is derived from teruma, as it is written concerning it: "and die in it if they profane it":

If so - For according to Rabbi Shimon, brother of Azarya, it came only to write: "and they shall not profane that which was set apart" [in the past tense]. What is written [using] a future tense verb "which they will set apart" means that this [other derivation] is also to be derived from it:
